e-5476.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $\mathbf{v}$ such that $A\mathbf{v}=\lambda \mathbf{v}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =4v.\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Determine if $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
after.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

If $v$ is an eigenvector, then there must exist a real number $\lambda $ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ Hence, we have

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=\lambda [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

This leads to the following system of equations for $\lambda :$

$$
{\begin{aligned}1=\lambda  \\ -2=-\lambda \end{aligned}
$$

This system has no solution. Therefore, $v$ is not an eigenvector of $A.$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Determine if $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
after.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

If $v$ is an eigenvector, then there must exist a real number $\lambda $ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ Hence, we have

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=\lambda [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

This leads to the following system of equations for $\lambda :$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2=2\lambda  \\ 3=-\lambda \end{aligned}
$$

This system has no solution. Therefore, $v$ is not an eigenvector of $A.$
